title: Full-Time, nine-month, tenure track position in Accounting | AY 2027-2028
description:
About the Job

APPOINTMENT START DATE: Appointment begins August 23, 2027;
classes begin August 30, 2027

APPLICATION REVIEW DATE: Review of complete applications
will begin on November 2nd, 2026, and continue until the position
is filled

ABOUT THE POSITION:

The Labovitz School of Business and Economics (LSBE) at the
University of Minnesota Duluth (UMD) invites applications for a
full-time, nine-month, tenure track, faculty position in the area
of Accounting at the Instructor/Assistant Professor level,
beginning Fall 2027.

The successful candidate will have responsibilities in teaching,
research, and service. Teaching responsibilities will include
undergraduate and graduate core and elective courses. The teaching
load is governed by the Collective Bargaining Agreement between the
University of Minnesota Board of Regents and the University
Education Association (UEA) and is currently five sections, or 15
credits, per academic year for research-active faculty. LSBE
courses are typically delivered in person, and the School values
opportunities for faculty to engage with industry through teaching,
research, and applied projects.

The successful candidate will be expected to maintain a
high-quality, impactful research program that produces scholarship
publishable in peer-reviewed journals and contributes meaningfully
to the discipline, professional practice, and/or society.

Service responsibilities will include advising undergraduate
students, supporting a student organization, and contributing to
the work of the department, School, University, community, and
relevant professional organizations. As a place-based institution,
LSBE values faculty presence on campus and expects faculty to
participate actively and in person in the academic and collegial
life of the School.

Qualifications

Required:


Candidates must be ABD (with their doctoral dissertation
defended by December 1, 2027) from an accredited university with a
curricular emphasis in the field of Accounting, or closely related
field. The applicant must have completed a minimum of two years in
residency during their program.
Candidates must have experience as instructor or teaching
assistant of at least one college level course.
Effective communication skills.
Strong evidence of potential for scholarship. The applicant
must demonstrate empirical research skills appropriate for, and
commitment to, developing a research stream in the field of
Accounting.



Preferred:


PhD or DBA from a school/college accredited by AACSB, EQUIS, or
AMBA, with a curricular emphasis in the field of Accounting.
Experience independently teaching multiple elective courses in
Accounting or closely related fields, at the undergraduate or
graduate level.
Experience or interest in teaching and / or research in the
areas of Auditing, Assurance or Forensic Accounting.
Full-time high level industry work experience. High level
experience is defined as holding a position with significant
operational decision-making and/or managerial oversight
authority.
Experience teaching courses with community embedded student
projects.
Published in peer-reviewed journals in the Accounting
area.
Professional certifications such as Certified Public Accountant
(CPA), Certified Management Accountant (CMA), or other relevant
certifications.
Demonstrated interpersonal skills necessary to effectively
fulfill service responsibilities to students, colleagues, the
department, school, campus, and community.
Demonstrated ability to incorporate artificial intelligence
(AI) related topics and/or tools in teaching that enhance
discipline specific industry applications.



About the Department

ABOUT LSBE:

The Labovitz School of Business and Economics (LSBE) is
AACSB-International accredited and housed in a state-of-the-art
building. Approximately 1,600 undergraduate and graduate students
are enrolled in the school’s programs. There are approximately 50
full-time faculty members in four academic departments: Accounting
and Finance, Economics and Health Care Management, Management
Studies, and Marketing. The School offers a Bachelor of Accounting,
Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Arts in Economics,
and MBA degrees. Regional outreach is accomplished primarily
through the Bureau of Business and Economic Research activities.
Additional information about the School and its programs can be
found on LSBE’s website at http://lsbe.d.umn.edu

Duluth, a vibrant city of approximately 88,000 residents, is
located at the western tip of beautiful Lake Superior. The city is
home to the Port of Duluth-Superior, the Great Lakes’ largest port
by tonnage, which welcomes more than 700 vessel visits and moves
more than 35 million tons of cargo annually. Duluth is also a major
tourism destination, attracting approximately 6.7 million visitors
each year, and offers exceptional access to outdoor recreation,
arts, culture, and year-round activities. The city serves as a
regional center for health care, anchored by two major healthcare
systems, and is home to a growing aviation and advanced
manufacturing sector that includes Cirrus Aircraft. Duluth is
served by its own commercial airport and is approximately a
2.5-hour drive from the Twin Cities metropolitan area. More
information about Duluth can be found at www.visitduluth.com .

Pay and Benefits

Pay Range: $130,000 - $140,000 annually; depending on
education/qualifications/experience

Time Appointment: 100% Appointment

Position Type: Faculty and P&A Staff

Please visit the Office of Human Resources website for more
information regarding benefit eligibility.

The University offers a comprehensive benefits package that
includes:

Competitive wages, paid holidays, and generous time off
Continuous learning opportunities through professional training
and degree-seeking programs supported by the Regents Tuition Benefit
Program
Low-cost medical, dental, and pharmacy plans
Healthcare and dependent care flexible spending accounts
University HSA contributions
Disability and employer-paid life insurance
Employee wellbeing program
Excellent retirement plans with employer contribution
Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF)
opportunity
Financial counseling services
Employee Assistance Program with eight sessions of counseling
at no cost

While our salary ranges provide a framework, it is important to
note that most of the
time, the initial pay may not reach the maximum of the range. This
approach ensures
that compensation reflects the value and unique contributions of
each candidate while
maintaining equity within our organization. As part of our
commitment to fair and
equitable compensation, please be aware that the salary offered to
incoming candidates
will be based on their individual credentials and experience.

How To Apply

Applications must be submitted online. To be considered for this
position, please click the Apply button and follow the
instructions. You will have the opportunity to complete an online
application for the position and attach a cover letter and resume
or CV.

To apply, please click here: http://employment.umn.edu/ and enter job
opening 376458 in Search Jobs. Follow the instructions to create an
online application for the position. Our employment system
requires that attached documents be uploaded as PDFs to fully
complete an application. Incomplete applications with missing
required documents may not be reviewed.

Required:


Current resume/curriculum vitae [follow prompt for additional
attachments after Resume section]. Include the following on your
uploaded resume/curriculum vitae: If ABD, include the month and
year of your dissertation proposal defense; if PhD or DBA, include
the month and year of your dissertation defense.
Cover letter/letter of interest
Graduate transcripts (official or unofficial)



Encouraged, when available:


A summary of qualitative and quantitative student evaluations
is encouraged when available. If you are submitting quantitative
analysis, fully describe any scales used; for example, lowest
possible score, highest possible score, and any preconstructed word
interpretations of the numerical values (such as 4 = “Agree” or
“Average”) [attach as “Other”]



Visa sponsorship, including H-1B, may be considered for
qualified candidates whose visa circumstances do not require
payment of the $100k H-1B fee

The Screening Committee will begin its review of complete
applications on November 2nd, 2026 and will continue until the
position is filled.

About University of Minnesota

University of Minnesota, Duluth (UMD)

The University of Minnesota, Duluth (UMD) consistently ranks among
the top Midwestern, regional universities in U.S. News and World
Report's "America's Best Colleges" issue.

Overlooking Lake Superior, UMD provides an alternative to both
large research and small liberal arts environments and attracts
students looking for a personalized learning experience on a
medium-sized campus of a major university. A firm liberal arts
foundation anchors a variety of traditional degree programs, as
well as professional and graduate students that draw on UMD's many
research institutes and labs.

At the University of Minnesota, we are proud to be recognized by
Forbes as a Best Employer for Company Culture (2026), Best Employer
for Women (2023, 2025, 2026), and Best Employer by State
(2022-2026). In 2026, we also received Culture Excellence &
Industry Awards recognition for employee appreciation and work-life
flexibility.
